# Independent evolution v1 interoperability fixture (v2 fitness vector — now an early-refusal witness)

`evolution-v1-kimi-k3max.base64` is a 4,024-byte, one-generation, non-terminal
history produced by the independent Kimi K3 Max implementation. It was not
generated by the implementation under test.

**ROLE CHANGE (PR 29, R2).** This artifact carries a **v2 fitness vector**, so
since fitness-vector v3 landed its successful-replay role is **historical**,
pinned to the pre-PR-29 commit (`a9d4468`, where it verified, resumed and
continued byte-identically to the terminal digest below). It is preserved as
an **early-refusal witness**: its framing, header digest, component digests,
generation chain and whole-history digest still verify, and the resume path
must then refuse it with `unsupportedVersion` naming `fitnessVectorVersion`
(stored 2, current 3) — after those self-consistency legs and before any
physics. The successful-replay role passed to
`evolution-v1-fitness-vector-v3-kimi.base64`, an independently assembled v3
artifact whose narrower, encoding-layer-only claim its own `.md` states
plainly.

The canonical config for its historical role was declared directly beside the
consuming Node and Chromium tests at the pre-PR-29 commit: population seed
`20260721`, terrain seed `20260722`, population 4, 60 steps, 3 generations,
deterministic physics, mutation probability `0.5`, and magnitude `0.1`.

At that commit the tests first required the local implementation's
generation-0 artifact to be byte-identical to this static fixture, then
resumed the static bytes and required the literal terminal continuation digest
above — intentionally stronger than an encode/decode round trip or a lock
regenerated by the same code. Since PR 29 the remaining assertions are the
refusal contract named above.
